findings.title: join() aborts cleanup of remaining flusher processes once the timeout budget is exhausted on an earlier process
findings.body: In join() the per-process wait/terminate loop (lines 337-347) uses `break` once `remaining_time <= 0` while iterating `self.processes.items()`. `break` exits the entire for-loop, not just the current iteration, so every flusher process that has not yet been visited in the dict is skipped completely: it is never waited on and `process.terminate()` is never called for it. Before this PR there was only one flusher process, so this had no visible effect. Now that there is one process per shard group (up to `max_processes`), if the deadline is exhausted while waiting on the first process(es) in the dict, the remaining per-shard flusher processes are left running un-terminated. Because they are daemon processes they will eventually die with the parent, but during controlled shutdown/rebalance they can keep producing to Kafka / polling Redis for shards that may already belong to another consumer instance, risking duplicate segment production and resource leaks.

findings.title: New isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard likely disables kill() for real flusher subprocesses
findings.body: _ensure_processes_alive() now wraps the restart kill with `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()` (lines 253-257). Previously this call was unconditional (`self.process.kill()`). Processes are spawned via `self.mp_context.Process` where `self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` (line 53), producing instances of `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. `multiprocessing.Process` (the bare module attribute used here) resolves to the *default* context's process class, which on platforms whose default start method is not 'spawn' (e.g. Linux defaults to 'fork') is a sibling class of `SpawnProcess`, not its superclass. In that case `isinstance(spawn_process_instance, multiprocessing.Process)` is False, so the new guard silently prevents `process.kill()` from ever running on real flusher subprocesses in production. A hung/unresponsive flusher process detected by the health check would then never actually be killed, while a brand-new replacement process is started for the same shards right away — leaving two processes concurrently operating on the same Redis shard/segment data, which can cause duplicate flush/production or resource exhaustion.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key "shards" vs "shard" for related flusher timers
findings.body: In SpanFlusher.main, the `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` timer and the `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` metric are tagged with `{"shard": shard_tag}` (lines 185 and 192-196), but the `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer right below uses `{"shards": shard_tag}` (line 199) for the exact same value. This tag-name typo means these two logically related metrics cannot be grouped or filtered consistently on the same tag in dashboards/alerts.

findings.title: Unused dead method _create_process_for_shard
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` (singular) is defined but never invoked. `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts crashed processes by directly calling `_create_process_for_shards` (plural) with the already-known `process_index`/`shards`, bypassing this helper entirely. This leftover method is unreachable dead code and should be removed or wired up if it was meant to be used.

findings.title: No validation of max_processes/flusher_processes allows silent fallback or a crash on invalid values
findings.body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `0` as falsy and silently substitutes the shard count, so passing `--flusher-processes 0` does not do what the operator asked. A negative value is not filtered out by `or` and flows into `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, which can become negative; `range(num_processes)` then produces an empty `process_to_shards_map`, and the subsequent `process_index = i % self.num_processes; self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` loop raises a `KeyError` because no entries exist. Neither the CLI option in src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py (plain `type=int`, no bounds) nor `SpanFlusher.__init__` validates for these cases.

findings.title: Docstring claims one process per shard, but shards can share a process when max_processes < shard count
findings.body: The updated class docstring states "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing," but the implementation caps processes at `max_processes` (the `flusher_processes` CLI option) and distributes shards round-robin across that smaller process count via `process_to_shards_map`. When `max_processes < len(assigned_shards)`, multiple shards share a single process/thread, contradicting the stated guarantee and potentially misleading operators tuning `--flusher-processes`.

findings.title: No test coverage for multi-process restart or multi-process join() timeout behavior
findings.body: The new test `test_flusher_processes_limit` only asserts that shards are distributed into the expected number of `process_to_shards_map` entries. It does not exercise `_ensure_processes_alive()` for the multi-process case (e.g. confirming that a crashed/hung process in one shard-group is restarted without disturbing other groups, or that kill()/restart actually works), nor does it exercise `join()` with a timeout while multiple processes are tracked (the path affected by the break-on-timeout issue in join()). Given this PR changes the flusher from a single background process to N per-shard-group processes, these newly introduced multi-process code paths are untested.

findings.title: Unrelated documentation change bundled into this PR
findings.body: The diff to CLAUDE.md adds an isinstance-vs-hasattr anti-pattern example that is unrelated to the span-buffer multiprocessed flusher feature this PR is about. Bundling unrelated doc changes into a feature PR increases review noise and makes it harder to bisect history for the actual feature change.
